epics.title: Accountable engineering loop
epics.objective: Enforce decision 0032 end to end: JIT frontier contracts gated at stage start, evidence-backed grills, bounded reviewable diffs.

tasks.title: Recorder refuses future execution detail
tasks.objective: record_decomposition_from_json.py refuses write_scope, required_tests, or verify_commands on any pending task after the earliest pending leaf, names the offending task and field, exempts completed tasks, and accepts detail on the frontier task. Existing test fixtures move to frontier-style recording.
acceptance_criteria: recording a decomposition with execution detail on a pending non-frontier task is refused with the task id and field named
the frontier task records detail successfully; completed tasks keep theirs (legacy cutover)
existing suite green after fixture migration

required_tests.command: uvx --with pytest --with psutil python3 -m pytest {path}::{id} -q -o junit_family=legacy --junitxml={report}
uvx --with pytest --with psutil python3 -m pytest {path}::{id} -q -o junit_family=legacy --junitxml={report}

tasks.reviewer_focus: Frontier resolution is the risky seam: the recorder's earliest-pending-leaf computation must agree with the protected stage authority in stages.py (status source of truth), or recorder and gates will disagree about which task may carry detail. Second seam: the done-task exemption is the legacy-cutover path - refusing a completed task's existing detail would brick every historical re-record. Refusal messages must name the offending task id and field. Fixture migration must not weaken existing gate coverage (tests that deliberately record full decompositions must still exercise their original refusal).

plan_contracts.statement: Recording execution detail (write_scope, required_tests, verify_commands) on a pending non-frontier task is refused with the task id and field named
The frontier task records detail successfully and completed tasks keep theirs (legacy cutover)
Existing suite is green after fixture migration with original refusal coverage preserved

tasks.title: Shared readiness gate at stage start and delegate
tasks.objective: require_ready_task() in factory_lib refuses an incomplete contract (write_scope, required_tests, verify_commands, reviewer_focus) or missing/stale task grill; stage start calls it before activating, delegate keeps it as defence in depth and refuses an active empty-scope stage instead of silently degrading to read-only.
acceptance_criteria: stage start refuses an incomplete or ungrilled frontier contract with a message naming the missing piece
delegate write runs re-check readiness; an active stage with empty write_scope refuses; explicit --read-only still passes

required_tests.command: uvx --with pytest --with psutil python3 -m pytest {path}::{id} -q -o junit_family=legacy --junitxml={report}
uvx --with pytest --with psutil python3 -m pytest {path}::{id} -q -o junit_family=legacy --junitxml={report}

tasks.reviewer_focus: Ordering is the risky seam: the readiness refusal in _cmd_start_locked must fire BEFORE any stage-state mutation and before the task_sha256 baseline stamp, or a refused start still pollutes measurement state. Second seam: delegate's write derivation - readiness re-check must precede launch for every write run; an active stage with empty write_scope refuses with a message naming the missing piece and the producing command; explicit --read-only stays exploration-only and must not satisfy stage done. Lite/quickfix/degraded behavior untouched. Self-application: this story's own T3 stage start runs through the new gate live - a wrong refusal wedges the loop.

plan_contracts.statement: stage start refuses an incomplete or ungrilled frontier contract, naming the missing piece
delegate re-checks readiness on write runs and refuses an active empty-scope stage
explicit --read-only delegation still passes and cannot close a stage

tasks.title: forge next routes the JIT loop; docs stop contradicting it
tasks.objective: forge next's implementing branch reports exactly one next action per frontier state (author contract, grill, stage start, delegate); docs/FACTORY.md, WORKFLOW.md, and factory/prompts/decomposer.md state the enforced JIT contract with no upfront-contract instruction remaining, and the author-contract action instructs entering plan mode per decision 0029 and planner.md.
acceptance_criteria: forge next output matches the frontier state machine for each of the four states
the author-contract next action tells the dev to enter plan mode for contract authoring
docs/FACTORY.md no longer instructs full upfront task contracts; WORKFLOW.md and decomposer.md are consistent with enforcement

required_tests.command: uvx --with pytest --with psutil python3 -m pytest {path}::{id} -q -o junit_family=legacy --junitxml={report}
uvx --with pytest --with psutil python3 -m pytest {path}::{id} -q -o junit_family=legacy --junitxml={report}

tasks.reviewer_focus: Single-action invariant is the risky seam: for the earliest unfinished task, forge next emits exactly ONE next action per state - skeleton contract -> enter plan mode, author the JIT contract, re-record (decisions 0029/0032); complete-but-ungrilled or stale -> run the task griller; fresh pass -> forge stage start; active -> forge delegate - never the current start+delegate pair. State must be DERIVED from the same primitives require_ready_task uses (a small non-raising task_frontier_state helper in factory_lib beside it; ACC-2's board rows consume the same helper), not recomputed independently. forge board's next_actions re-parse must keep working. Docs edits (FACTORY.md upfront-contract list, WORKFLOW/decomposer digest wording, forge skill task-loop, AGENTS.md narration line sharpened per conduct s8) must remove the contradiction without weakening any other stated contract.

plan_contracts.statement: forge next reports author-contract (with plan-mode instruction) / grill / stage-start / delegate as the single next action per frontier state
docs/FACTORY.md, WORKFLOW.md, and factory/prompts/decomposer.md state the enforced JIT contract with no upfront-contract instruction remaining
